'Progressive hearing loss' (Classic findings of osteogenesis imperfecta) also fits 'Late congenital-syphilis stigmata' (CN VIII deafness), and 'Sensorineural deafness' can occur in OI, so the two hearing-loss tiles are near-interchangeable
'Marked neutrophilia' (Findings of leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1) also fits 'Chronic myeloid-leukemia clues' (marked neutrophilic leukocytosis is a classic CML presentation)

'Isoniazid' (Classic initial RIPE tuberculosis drugs) also fits 'Contributors to niacin deficiency' (isoniazid-induced B6 depletion is a textbook cause of pellagra, and 'Vitamin B6 deficiency' is already on that group)

'Elevated IgE' (ABPA findings) also fits 'IgE-associated immune events' 'Type I hypersensitivity' (IgE-associated immune events) also fits 'Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis findings' (ABPA is a type I/III hypersensitivity), so the two tiles can be swapped and both groups stay valid

'Campylobacter jejuni' and 'Yersinia enterocolitica' (Unpasteurized dairy) fit 'Enteric triggers of reactive arthritis' exactly as well as 'Campylobacter' and 'Yersinia', which are interchangeable with them 'Campylobacter' and 'Yersinia' (Reactive arthritis) equally fit 'Bacterial infections linked to unpasteurized dairy' 'Salmonella' (Reactive arthritis) is also a classic raw-milk pathogen

PLX-BCH-033 note ('keep other glucogenic amino acids off the board') is violated: Serine, Threonine, Asparagine and Glutamine (Polar uncharged amino acids) are all glucogenic and fit 'Carbon sources for gluconeogenesis' alongside Alanine; glutamine in particular is a major gluconeogenic substrate

'Microvascular thrombosis' (Hyperacute graft rejection clues) is the defining lesion of Shiga-toxin HUS (thrombotic microangiopathy) and fits 'Shiga-toxin-associated HUS clues' as well, while 'Acute kidney injury' (HUS) fits hyperacute rejection of a kidney graft, giving a defensible swap

'Pancytopenia' (Visceral leishmaniasis) is the defining feature of Fanconi anemia and fits 'Fanconi anemia associations' as well, while 'Bone marrow failure' (Fanconi) is near-synonymous and VL causes marrow involvement, so the two tiles are interchangeable

'Elevated IgE' (ABPA findings) also fits 'IgE-associated immune events', and 'Type I hypersensitivity' (IgE-associated immune events) also fits 'Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis findings' (ABPA is a type I/III hypersensitivity); swapping the two gives a second defensible partition

'Serine', 'Threonine', 'Asparagine' and 'Glutamine' (Polar uncharged amino acids) are all glucogenic amino acids and fit 'Carbon sources for gluconeogenesis' (glutamine is a major gluconeogenic substrate) alongside 'Alanine' PLX-BCH-033 instruction to keep other glucogenic amino acids off the board is violated by the polar uncharged group

'Campylobacter' and 'Yersinia' (Enteric triggers of reactive arthritis) are the same organisms as 'Campylobacter jejuni' and 'Yersinia enterocolitica' (unpasteurized dairy), so each pair can be swapped freely between the two groups 'Salmonella' (reactive arthritis) also fits 'Bacterial infections linked to unpasteurized dairy' (raw milk is a classic Salmonella source)

"Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome" (X-linked inborn errors of immunity) also fits "Mucocutaneous bleeding from primary-hemostasis defects": WAS causes thrombocytopenia with small platelets, which produces petechiae and mucocutaneous bleeding. "Eczema" (Classic phenylketonuria presentation clues) is part of the classic Wiskott-Aldrich triad, which strengthens the pull toward the X-linked group.

"Anaphylaxis after cyst rupture" (Hydatid disease diagnostic and complication clues) also fits "IgE-associated immune events": it is IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity to released antigen, and 'Helminth defense' could plausibly be swapped into the hydatid group.

"Weight loss" (VIPoma (Verner-Morrison) findings) also fits "Characteristic associations of Graves disease": weight loss is a hallmark of Graves hyperthyroidism, and it is not part of the classic WDHA triad.

"Thrombocytopenia" (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome clues) is a defensible member of Characteristic Gaucher disease findings: thrombocytopenia from hypersplenism and marrow infiltration is a classic presenting Gaucher finding (bruising/bleeding).

"Massive splenomegaly" (Myelofibrosis clues) fits Visceral leishmaniasis diagnostic associations: kala-azar is a classic cause of massive splenomegaly, making it near-interchangeable with "Hepatosplenomegaly". "Hepatosplenomegaly" (Visceral leishmaniasis diagnostic associations) fits Myelofibrosis clues: extramedullary hematopoiesis enlarges both liver and spleen.

"Foul-smelling fatty diarrhea" (Giardiasis clinical and microscopy clues) fits Diagnostic pattern of chronic pancreatic exocrine insufficiency: steatorrhea is the defining clinical feature of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

"Vitamin B12 deficiency" (Potentially treatable contributors to cognitive impairment) fits Consequences of parietal-cell autoimmunity: pernicious anemia directly causes B12 deficiency, near-interchangeable with "Vitamin B12 malabsorption". "Megaloblastic anemia", "Hypersegmented neutrophils" and "Increased homocysteine" (Folate-deficiency laboratory pattern) are also consequences of parietal-cell autoimmunity via B12 deficiency.

"Meckel diverticulum" (Potential lead points for intussusception) also fits Sources of chronic iron-loss anemia: ectopic gastric mucosa causes painless GI bleeding and is a classic cause of iron-deficiency anemia in children. "Intestinal polyp" (Potential lead points for intussusception) also fits Sources of chronic iron-loss anemia: bleeding GI polyps are a standard cause of occult blood loss and iron deficiency, nearly interchangeable with "Bleeding gastrointestinal malignancy".

"Escherichia coli" (Bacterial pathogens of infectious epididymitis) also fits Bacterial infections linked to unpasteurized dairy: E. coli O157:H7 (EHEC) is a classic raw-milk pathogen, as the MICRO-010 flag itself notes.

"Scleroderma" (Conditions predisposing to gastroesophageal reflux) also fits Characteristic limited systemic sclerosis features: it names the disease itself, so the player sees five systemic-sclerosis tiles, and the esophageal dysmotility it implies is the CREST feature the MSK-017 flag warns against placing on the board.

"Factor V Leiden" (Inherited venous-thrombophilia mechanisms) also fits Category 4 contraindications to combined (estrogen-containing) hormonal contraception: known thrombogenic mutations are US MEC Category 4 and a classic USMLE estrogen contraindication; the same applies to "Prothrombin G20210A mutation", "Antithrombin deficiency" and "Protein C deficiency".

"IBD-associated (enteropathic) spondyloarthritis" (Seronegative spondyloarthritides) is itself an extraintestinal manifestation of IBD and fits "Extraintestinal manifestations of inflammatory bowel disease" as well as its own group; "Sacroiliitis" is the axial lesion of that same entity, so the two are near-interchangeable.

"Ketonemia" (Classic clues to diabetic ketoacidosis) fits "Metabolic consequences of ethanol-driven NADH excess" because alcoholic ketoacidosis produces ketonemia. "Anion gap metabolic acidosis" (Classic clues to diabetic ketoacidosis) fits "Metabolic consequences of ethanol-driven NADH excess" because ethanol-driven lactic acidosis and ketoacidosis are both anion-gap acidoses.

"Achlorhydria" (VIPoma (Verner-Morrison) findings) fits "Consequences of parietal-cell autoimmunity" equally well: autoimmune destruction of parietal cells abolishes acid secretion, a classic consequence of autoimmune atrophic gastritis.

"Thrombocytopenia" (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome clues) is itself a primary-hemostasis defect causing mucocutaneous bleeding, so it fits "Mucocutaneous bleeding from primary-hemostasis defects" (especially beside "Immune thrombocytopenia" and BSS, which is often thrombocytopenic).
